subject: pathology
title: Post-Streptococcal GN, Subepithelial Humps, and IgA Nephropathy Mesangial Deposits

steps.tx: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis follows nephritogenic streptococcal throat or skin infection by latent weeks, immune complexes swelling children with haematuria, oedema, hypertension, and low C3 recovering usually. That latent nephritis is **post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN)**. Skin infection gives a longer latent period, often three to six weeks, compared with one to three weeks after pharyngitis.
steps.say: Cola urine, swollen face, high pressure two weeks after strep throat in a child means PSGN.

steps.tx: Subepithelial humps, large immune deposits bulging beneath podocytes on electron microscopy with endocapillary neutrophils, sign postinfectious glomerulonephritis under glass. Those humps are the **subepithelial humps of postinfectious GN**. Immunofluorescence shows granular IgG and C3 in a starry sky pattern along capillary walls and mesangium.
steps.say: Humps on the epithelial side mean postinfectious deposits; neutrophils flooding capillaries agree.

steps.tx: Electron microscopy zooms past what light microscopy can resolve and finds the deposit that settles this diagnosis. A single huge hump bulges beneath the podocyte, lifting it away from the capillary wall on the urinary side. That protrusion is the **subepithelial hump** of postinfectious glomerulonephritis, built from immune complexes planted after streptococcal infection. Between the humps, neutrophils crowd the capillary lumens, matching the sudden nephritic picture of cola coloured urine and swelling in a recovering child.
steps.say: A large subepithelial hump on electron microscopy is the deposit that defines postinfectious glomerulonephritis.

vis.caption: Postinfectious glomerulonephritis electron microscopy with subepithelial humps. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: IgA nephropathy deposits polymeric IgA in mesangium world wide, synpharyngitic haematuria arriving with sore throats within days, mesangial hypercellularity and Oxford scores staging progression. The mesangial disease is **IgA nephropathy (Berger disease)**. It is the commonest primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, especially in East Asian and European populations.
steps.say: Visible blood with the sore throat, not weeks after, is IgA nephropathy signing its timing.

vis.caption: IgA nephropathy pathogenesis from galactose deficient IgA to mesangial deposits.

steps.tx: Galactose deficient IgA forms immune complexes with anti-glycan antibodies depositing mesangially and activating complement, a four hit model explaining familial and mucosal associations. That model is the **four-hit pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy**. The Oxford MEST-C score grades mesangial and endocapillary cellularity, sclerosis, tubular atrophy and crescents on biopsy.
steps.say: Defective IgA sugar, anti-sugar antibodies, complexes, mesangial injury: IgA nephropathy in four hits.

steps.tx: IgA vasculitis, Henoch-Schonlein, shares mesangial IgA with systemic small vessel disease of skin, gut, and joints, kidney histology indistinguishable from IgA nephropathy. That systemic sibling is **IgA vasculitis nephritis versus IgA nephropathy**. Palpable purpura over buttocks and legs with colicky abdominal pain is the classic extrarenal presentation in children.
steps.say: Palpable purpura plus mesangial IgA is IgA vasculitis; kidney alone keeps the nephropathy name.

vis.alt: IgA vasculitis palpable purpura and mesangial IgA
vis.caption: IgA vasculitis with lower limb palpable purpura and glomerular mesangial IgA deposition, the systemic sibling of IgA nephropathy.

steps.tx: Persistent low C3 beyond eight to twelve weeks after apparent PSGN rewrites differential toward C3 glomerulopathy or lupus, demanding biopsy rather than continued reassurance. That deadline is **persistent hypocomplementaemia after postinfectious GN**. In uncomplicated PSGN, C3 typically returns to normal by six to eight weeks from presentation.
steps.say: C3 still low at twelve weeks is not slow PSGN recovery; biopsy toward C3 disease or lupus.

steps.tx: Supportive care, salt restriction, diuretics, pressure control, and streptococcal eradication treat most childhood PSGN without immunosuppression unless crescents supervene. Restraint defines **supportive management of post-streptococcal GN**. Loop diuretics control the volume driven hypertension of acute nephritis far better than vasodilators alone.
steps.say: Most childhood PSGN needs diuretics, salt sense, and time, not steroids; crescents change that.

steps.tx: IgA nephropathy therapy now layers optimised RAAS and SGLT2 support, targeted budesonide for intestinal immune modulation, and trials for high risk proteinuria despite support. That layering is **contemporary IgA nephropathy therapy**. Targeted release budesonide acts at ileal Peyer's patches, reducing production of the galactose deficient IgA itself.
steps.say: Support first, then gut targeted budesonide and trials select IgA patients still leaking protein.
